cards.title: Introduction to Web Development
cards.content: As a Python developer, understanding web development involves bridging the gap between Python backend frameworks (like Django or FastAPI) and frontend technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) that run in the browser.

options.text: GET is used to send sensitive data securely in the URL.
POST is typically used to send data to create or update a resource.
PUT is used exclusively for deleting resources.
DELETE cannot be handled by standard web browsers.

cards.title: HTML and CSS Essentials
cards.content:
HTML provides the structure of a webpage, while CSS handles the styling.

<div class="container">
  <h1>Hello World</h1>
</div>

CSS:

.container {
  background-color: #f0f0f0;
}

pairs.right: Modern, fast API framework with automatic docs

content.text: To select an element by its ID in JavaScript, we commonly use the document._____('my-id') method.

steps.text: Client enters URL and browser sends an HTTP request.
Web server receives request and routes it to the Python application.
Python code processes business logic and queries database.
Server returns an HTTP response containing HTML/JSON.
Browser renders the response for the user.

cards.title: Conclusion
cards.content: You now have a foundational understanding of how web development concepts map to Python development. Continue building full-stack applications to solidify these skills!
